title: Siegard trace file
description: What ties a delivered file back to the specification node it was written to satisfy, after the plan that wrote it is gone: `siegard-trace.json`, beside `siegard.json` at the git toplevel of the target source root. Planning and delivery are disposable by design — a task exists to get code written, and nothing requires it to survive that — so this is the one fact this framework keeps once the plan is deleted: for a node it has bound, the digest it read and the file(s) it produced, each pinned the same way. A later run recomputes both digests from what is on disk now and compares: a node whose digest no longer matches moved in the specification since this entry was written; a file whose digest no longer matches moved in the code without a matching rebind. Either is drift, and this file is what makes it checkable without any plan's history to consult. Nobody hand-authors an entry — `bin/trace.py` is the one writer, computing both digests itself at bind time, and the one reader that recomputes them to report drift.

specification.description: The specification root every node below is an identity into — «Identity is the node's path from the specification root, without `.md`» (SPEC-003 R1) — by path relative to this file's own directory. Every binding in this file traces against the one specification named here; tracing against a second one is a second trace file, never a second entry.

bindings.description: One entry per specification node this project has bound to code, at most one each — a node bound twice is one binding with a stale copy sitting beside it, and bin/trace.py refuses that rather than pick a side.

node.description: The specification node's identity — «Identity is the node's path from the specification root, without `.md`» (SPEC-003 R1): its path under `specification`.

digest.description: The node's content digest as `bin/trace.py --bind` read it, the same value `spec.py --digest` computes for it. Diverging from what the node computes to now says the specification moved since this binding was written — the files below may no longer be what the node asks for.

files.description: Every file this node's binding produced or governs, each pinned at the digest it held when this entry was last written. Held whatever decides the binding: where the node's fact lives is a question the source answers and a test cannot, and `--encodes` reads it from here.

decided_by.description: What settles whether this node's fact still holds when one of its files moves. Absent or `reading`: a conformance judgment reads the node against the file, which is every binding's default and how every binding was written before this field existed. `test`: a test the project's own suite runs decides it — one a judgment certified, once, as a test that would fail if the fact stopped holding — so a later drift on `files` is answered by that step's run rather than by a fresh reading. It is written only from a record whose judgment certified the test, never declared by hand, and never inferred from a node's type: whether a fact is one a test decides is read off the fact's own outcome. A green run says the fact holds; it says nothing about which file holds it, which is why `files` stays and its digests still report.

step.description: Which step of the project's registry runs the proof, by the name `commands[].step` gives it. The runner, the command and its bound are the registry's; this names the step and nothing about how it runs, exactly as a standard rule's `tool` does.

proof.description: The test file(s) the certification named, each pinned at the digest it held when certified. A test whose digest no longer matches is drift of its own class: the certification was of that text, and a test that changed may no longer fail when the fact stops holding — so the binding is decided by reading again until a judgment certifies the test as it now stands.

allOf.$comment: A binding a test decides names the test and the step that runs it, or it is not one; a binding a reading decides names neither. The join is structural so that a binding cannot claim a test it does not point at, nor point at one while claiming a reading decides it.

path.description: Relative to this file's own directory, the same anchor `specification` uses — never absolute, and never relative to whatever directory a tool happened to run from.

digest.description: The file's content digest as `bin/trace.py --bind` read it. Diverging from what the file computes to now says the code changed without a rebind — an edit this trace does not yet know about, not necessarily a wrong one.

judged.description: Present only where a reconciliation's judgment cleared this pair at this digest: `--bind-record` writes it when the record it binds from is a reconciliation. Absent means the pair was stamped by a delivery or by hand and has not been read against the node since. A review's staging omits a pair only where it is present, and a later bind of the pair from an implementation record or by hand writes the entry without it.

pin.description: Content identity: the SHA-256 of the bytes of whatever this field's owner names, written `sha256:<hexdigest>` and computable by hand with `sha256sum`.
